Configure multiple-choice scoring

Source: R/multiple_choice_scoring.R
multiple_choice_scoring.Rd

Create a scoring specification for multipleChoice() or a multiple-choice Rmd item. These items permit several selected options. For one-answer items, see single_choice_scoring(). Both this helper and the multiple-choice item default to "standard": balanced partial credit equivalent to Youden's J with a zero floor for the usual automatically balanced weights.

Usage

multiple_choice_scoring(method = "standard", ...)

Arguments

method

A multiple-choice method. See the table below. The default is "standard". Single-choice penalties and the kanzow_* presets are not accepted by this helper.

...

Settings for the selected method. weights and plus_minus accept lower_bound (default 0), a nonpositive fraction of the maximum. all_or_nothing accepts incorrect (default 0) and omitted (default 0), also fractions of the maximum. exams accepts partial (default TRUE), negative (default FALSE), and rule (false2, false, true, all, or none), reproducing exams::exams_eval() for multiple-choice items.

Value

A named list for scoring_scheme in multipleChoice(). Passing it to singleChoice() is an error. Plain YAML mappings are interpreted using the item's type.

Methods

Positive entries in the item's points identify correct options, and their sum is the maximum score P. C is the number of correct options and W the number of incorrect options.

MethodRule
standardDefault balanced (Youden's J) weights and zero floor; explicit weights are preserved
weightsPreserve all supplied weights, including explicit zeros; use the chosen floor
all_or_nothingFull credit only for selecting exactly the correct set
plus_minusEach selected correct option adds P/C; each selected incorrect option subtracts P/C
subsetSelected correct options earn P/C each, only if no incorrect option is selected
ripkeySelected correct options earn P/C each, unless more than C options are selected
true_falseEach correctly classified option earns P/(C+W), including unchecked incorrect options
examsUse the selected R/exams weighting, partial-credit setting and score floor

The five literature methods are described by Betts et al. Their raw scores are scaled here to the item maximum P. Those five methods and exams use the correct-option set and its total points, rather than the relative magnitudes of positive option weights. standard and weights preserve individual contributions, with the zero-weight handling described above.

Default

balanced scoring and Youden's J: With C > 0 correct options, W > 0 incorrect options, equal correct-option weights, and automatically balanced incorrect-option penalties, the raw normalized score is Youden's J: $$J = \frac{\#\mathrm{correct\ options\ selected}}{C} - \frac{\#\mathrm{incorrect\ options\ selected}}{W}.$$ The awarded score is \(P\max(0,J)\). Each selected correct option adds P/C and each selected incorrect option subtracts P/W; unchecked options contribute zero. This is the ordinary Rmd default when its correct options share the points equally. The raw J has zero expectation under independent random selection; flooring it at zero does not preserve that expectation. standard also preserves explicit negative option weights. If the positive or negative weights differ from those balanced contributions, the resulting custom weighting is not necessarily Youden's J. standard is the method identifier; Youden's J describes its ordinary balanced special case.

Empty responses and bounds

true_false treats an unchecked option as a false decision, so an empty selection can earn P*W/(C+W). Checkboxes cannot distinguish a deliberate nonselection from an omitted decision. An explicit true/false/omission interaction is a different format. The other methods score an empty response as zero unless otherwise configured. By default negative totals are floored at zero; weights, plus_minus, all_or_nothing, and exams can allow negative scores through their documented settings. Scores never exceed P.

Rmd/YAML

scoring_scheme:
  method: exams
  partial: true
  negative: -0.25
  rule: "false2"

Or use a preset string, for example scoring_scheme: plus_minus. The YAML list is interpreted from type: mpc (or another supported multiple-choice type alias); no function call is needed inside YAML.

References

Betts J, Muntean W, Kim D, Kao S (2022). Evaluating Different Scoring Methods for Multiple Response Items Providing Partial Credit. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 82(1), 151–176. doi:10.1177/0013164421994636.

See also

multipleChoice(), single_choice_scoring()

Examples

multipleChoice(choices = c("A", "B", "C"), points = c(0.5, 0, 0.5),
  scoring_scheme = multiple_choice_scoring("plus_minus"))
